statements.t: We expect a final decision by the FDA on our PMA by early first quarter of 2027.
We expect to continue to incur operating losses for at least the next several years as we invest in research and development and the commercialization of existing products.
We believe there are several important factors that have impacted and that we expect will impact our operating performance and results of operations, including:
Our performance will be impacted by the extent to which we can secure reimbursement and coverage for Galleri.

Prior to broader coverage and reimbursement in the United States, we will continue our work with clinics, health systems, and digital health platforms to accelerate utilization, and with self-insured employers and health insurers to offer and cover Galleri.

The FDA convenes advisory committees to obtain independent expert advice and is not bound by the advisory committee’s recommendations, though it takes such recommendations into consideration when making its final decision on our PMA, which is expected by early first quarter of 2027.

If we obtain FDA approval, we expect to pursue coverage through this new law and, subsequently, inclusion of Galleri in the United States Preventive Services Task Force (“USPSTF”) guideline recommendation, although such inclusion may take years and is not certain even with FDA approval.
We believe the decision will include considerations such as NHS budget, political priorities, cost-effectiveness and implementation constraints in addition to an evaluation of the final results.
We expect to continue selectively engaging with international opportunities over time.

Our ability to expand into new regions and jurisdictions, drive commercial sales and growth within those regions and jurisdictions and navigate economic, political, regulatory, and other risks, including geopolitical conflict associated with international operations, will be an important driver of our performance.

We make significant efforts to educate these key stakeholders regarding the benefits of MCED and the clinical and economic value of our products, which we believe will continue to drive awareness of MCED and expand the commercial opportunity for our products.
There has been a significant increase in competition in the market for MCED testing and in cancer screening tests generally, and we expect this trend of increasing competition to continue.
Over the last few years, a number of new MCED and cancer screening products have launched commercially, and we expect additional products to launch in the future.

While we believe that increasing competition, including the addition of new market entrants and products, will help develop our target market, these competitors generally compete with us for customers on the basis of test performance, ease of use and pricing and have created a more crowded competitive market than previously existed.
Our ability to differentiate Galleri from competitors is and will remain a key factor in determining our success.
A key factor to our future success is and will be our ability to increase demand for, and sales of, Galleri from new and existing customers.

Our commercial strategy targets primary care physicians, health systems, employers, digital health platforms, payors, international distributors and life insurance providers, and focuses on innovative value-oriented partnerships.
We expect the September 2026 pricing promotion to continue to impact our average selling price (“ASP”) in the coming periods.
As part of our overall pricing strategy, we expect these rates, discounts, rebates and promotions to reduce our ASP over time.
We also expect to increase demand from new customers through our efforts to further develop the market for MCED testing.
We believe these studies are critical to driving adoption of our tests, as well as favorable coverage decisions, and expect to continue investment in data generation.

We expect research and development expenses to decrease over the next three years as several of our large clinical trials transition to long-term follow-up, and development of our automated platform has substantially concluded.

We will continue to invest in Galleri, including generating and reporting clinical utility evidence to support broad adoption, progressing our PMA towards potential approval, innovating to further improve Galleri’s test performance while reducing cost, and we will evaluate other research and development opportunities from time to time.

As demand for our products increases, we expect to further leverage the scale efficiencies of our infrastructure and platform technology, which we believe will positively impact Galleri margins over time.
This version incorporates a highly-automated industrial scale platform and is intended to enable us to scale more efficiently with future demand.

For self-pay patients, we have concluded that an implied contract exists, however the transaction price for the implied contract represents variable consideration as there are situations in which we do not expect to collect the full invoiced amounts from self-pay patients due to price concessions.
We utilize the expected value approach to estimate the transaction price and apply a constraint for such variable consideration, on a portfolio basis.

These margin improvements from scale efficiencies will at least be partially offset when we commence recognition of royalties owing under the terms of the Illumina Supply Agreement on December 24, 2026 as well as by anticipated reductions in ASP due to pricing reductions over time through list price changes, discounts, rebates, promotions or other pricing activity.

We currently expect research and development expenses to decrease over the next three years as several of our large clinical trials transition to long-term follow-up, and development of our automated platform has substantially concluded.

We expect our sales and marketing expense s to increase as we invest in initiatives to drive awareness and demand generation of Galleri and to decrease as a percentage of revenue over the next three years and long term.

We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase as we continue to invest in corporate infrastructure to support public company operations and the commercialization of Galleri and to decrease as a percentage of revenue over the next three years and long term.
Additionally, it is not intended to be a measure of free cash flow for management’s discretionary use, as it does not consider certain cash requirements such as interest and tax payments.
Under the terms of the Illumina Supply Agreement, regardless of whether our products incorporate any Illumina technology, we will be obligated to pay Illumina a royalty.
We expect that the royalty payments we will make to Illumina in the foreseeable future will result in a 7% royalty rate.

We expect to continue to incur operating losses over at least the next several years as we continue to invest in research and development and seek to achieve broad reimbursement of our current commercialized products.
However, we anticipate that we will need to raise additional financing in the future to fund our operations.

To evaluate recoverability, we compare the carrying amount of the asset to the amount of consideration we expect to receive, and that has not been recognized as revenue in exchange for the goods or services to which the asset relates, less the costs that relate directly to providing those goods or services and that have not yet been recognized as expenses.
We expect to cease to be an EGC effective December 31, 2026.

estimates.name: Assessment for Recoverability and Impairment
estimates.t: The recoverability assessment requires significant judgment and is based on estimates of future revenues, costs, and other assumptions regarding the expected performance of the underlying arrangement.

estimates.name: JOBS Act
estimates.t: We are an emerging growth company (“EGC”) under the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of 2012 (the “JOBS Act”).
